summary: 44 of 49 required checks pass. Build (9/9), Inspection (12/12), Spec (7/7), and Visual (9/9 via S6 snapshot baselines + iOS empirical) are all green. Group BX (behavior + conformance) is the failure surface: 7/12 pass — BX1, BX2, BX5 (the three load-bearing reactive invariants), BX7, BX10, BX11, BX12 all pass empirically — but BX3 (toggle), BX4 (slider), BX6 (form row height), BX8 (sheet), BX9 (button height) fail. None of the failures invalidate the SwiftKit bridge architecture; the three reactive invariants prove the trampoline + reactive label mutator chain works end-to-end on both platforms. The 5 BX failures decompose into (a) two Crystal-side crashes inside specific probe slugs — BX4 is sprintf Float64 panic in UI::Probes::SliderProbe::formatted (Crystal Float printer / RyuPrintf) and BX8 is NULL string reaching apsk_nsstring during sheet slug initial render; (b) two SwiftUI-hosting-frame layout failures BX6 and BX9 where UIHostingController is sized at 25.125pt instead of SwiftUI's intrinsic 44pt; (c) one UIHostingController hit-test propagation failure on BX3 toggle. All five are integration-level bugs, NOT architectural gaps in the bridge — the macOS twin BX7 passes, BX10 dark-mode tint shift passes, BX5 runtime override re-render passes — confirming the bridge wiring is correct and the iOS failures are bounded to (1) the Crystal Float printer + NULL-string guard in two probe-specific code paths and (2) the iOS UIHostingController sizing/hit-test integration.
